audit.whatIsWrong: Row 2 gave Yasuo a bracket its own whys[2] calls "an even, timing-based skill matchup", and row 6 gave Yasuo the 2-item bracket while whys[6], spikes[3] and late all say Vladimir becomes unkillable there.
audit.why: The mirror (vladimir__yasuo) set row 2 to Skill at 5/10 and row 6 to Vladimir at 7/10; inverted, that is Skill 5/10 and Vladimir 3/10 here, and it agrees with the packet chart and with this page's prose.
audit.corrected: Rows 2 and 6 flipped in BOTH layers as one atomic group with matching ratings, and phases[6].why rewritten so the explanation matches the side.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2-item stage was described as Yasuo's side-lane peak with no mention of what actually spikes for Vladimir.
audit.why: Crimson Pact converts bonus health into AP and back, so every defensive item he buys is also damage; Hemoplague is a flat 120s amp-and-heal.
audit.corrected: phases[6].why now names the Hemoplague and Crimson Pact scaling, and dontsFull[1].d explains why raw crit is the wrong response.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three do/don't bodies were generic boilerplate that did not match their titles, and none of them carried Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds of untargetability, its 28s rank-1 cooldown, or the Grievous Wounds requirement.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags needs-antiheal on Transfusion (Q, 9/7.9/6.8/5.7/4.6s) and Hemoplague (R). Sanguine Pool's untargetable window is what eats Last Breath, and Last Breath needs an airborne target, so a pooled Vladimir cancels the whole pattern. Wind Wall blocks none of his kit — no Vladimir ability carries the projectile flag, and the page correctly says so in spikes[2].
audit.corrected: dosFull[1].d now gives the 28s/2s numbers and the bait-then-EQ-R order, dosFull[2].d names Transfusion's cooldown and Grievous Wounds, dontsFull[0].d states what the untargetability eats, dontsFull[1].d names Crimson Pact.
